main_body: Two-storey timber-frame house: a large shingled roof slope over a plaster and half-timber upper wall, with a stone-block ground floor and door
top_band: Mid-brown shingle roof slope in rows 1-43 down the centre column, with lighter shingle highlights along the top edge and a dark eave line in rows 43-45
evidence: The roof is drawn as a large sloped surface with a hipped silhouette and a dark eave band at rows 43-45, directly above the vertical wall face. The wall face runs from row 46 to row 106. The windows and the door have dark inner edges and sills, so they read as inset. The roof top is much larger than a thin rim, and a building roof counts as its top surface. This matches the reference houses, so it reads as 3/4.

style.evidence: The palette is about 4-5 tones: dark maroon, mid brown, tan and cream. The roof shingles are a patterned dither of one brown on dark, with only a few light pixels, so there is no per-tile highlight ramp like the references. The plaster panels are large flat cream areas, 10x10 pixels or more, with no speckle. The stone ground floor has a block pattern but only 2-3 tones. The outline is a dark reddish brown rather than pure black, which is acceptable. Overall it is clearly flatter and has fewer colours per tile than the Beodeul houses.
